reason: I'd maybe download it and try the free first summary before my appointment, but I'm not paying anything until I've seen whether my doctor actually takes it seriously. On $20k a year I already spend on supplements, so another app charge has to prove itself first.
objection: Every period app says it's private. Flo said stuff too. 'Runs on your phone' sounds good, but I don't know who you are or how I'd actually check that my data isn't going anywhere.
would_change_my_mind: If the free summary actually got my doctor to order the right tests and take my symptoms seriously, I'd pay the $7.99 for the next appointment without thinking twice.
